clue.text: Unyielding girl meets older boy to talk initially

indicators.note: initially points at the opening of the neighbouring word, so only its start is taken

parts.note: a girl's name
a boy grown older becomes a grown male
the opening letter of talk

explanation.surface: A determined girl meets an older boy for a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant describes someone who refuses to be persuaded or change their position, firmly unbending.

clue.text: Nearly left in a moment, by the way

indicators.note: by means beside or next to, so the last piece is set alongside
in places one item inside another, so the left sits within the moment

parts.note: a mo is a short moment
L is the abbreviation for left
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone nearly went in an instant, incidentally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' looks like an aside, but by places the street abbreviation alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and nearly are synonyms meaning not quite fully.

clue.text: Dress, but become weary after a short time

indicators.note: after says the weary verb comes later in the order than the short-time pieces

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
to tire is to grow weary

explanation.surface: Someone gets dressed but soon grows bored of the outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire means clothing or garments, a noun equal to dress in general.

clue.text: When to leave port workers to attackers

parts.note: as in the sense of when, as in 'as I left'
ships sail when they leave port
worker ants, a crossword staple for workers

explanation.surface: Dock labourers are told when to quit the harbour to face attackers.
explanation.definitionFit: Assailants are people who attack someone physically or verbally.

clue.text: Let it out, sir!

indicators.note: let out suggests setting free, and freed letters fall into a fresh order

parts.note: the two words taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone urges a gentleman to release something, perhaps a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is an honorific form of address, an example of a rank or honour attached to a name.

clue.text: Take advantage to get out when Arab group invades

indicators.note: an invader pushes into territory, so the group goes inside the other word

parts.note: an exit is the way out
the Palestine Liberation Organisation

explanation.surface: Someone escapes while an Arab faction storms in, seizing the chance.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it for one's own benefit, often unfairly.

clue.text: Speed, as I see unfortunately going around, means stress

indicators.note: going around means encircling, so the jumbled letters wrap the speed unit
something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters come out of order

parts.note: taken as letters to be rearranged
miles per hour, a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A driver regrets speeding around, which causes stress.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to give it special weight or importance, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Young boxer, maybe, requires a period of development

definitions.note: the pupa is the creature in that stage rather than the stage itself

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, and a young dog is a puppy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novice fighter needs time to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is the dog breed, not the fighter; 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupa is the insect in its resting stage between larva and adult, while it transforms.

clue.text: Following orders to live and die, not rioting around

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the living and dying words
a riot is disorder, so the neighbouring letters are thrown into chaos

parts.note: taken as letters to be rearranged
to be is to exist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier told to live or die by command, without rebelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not rioting' reads as peaceful, but rioting jumbles the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An obedient person complies with instructions, which is exactly doing as one is told.

clue.text: Most delicious wine in the trial

indicators.note: in places the wine inside the trial word

parts.note: a test is a trial
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: The finest-tasting wine at a tasting competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastiest is the superlative of tasty, meaning having the best flavour.

clue.text: Friends scoffed about writing

indicators.note: about in the sense of surrounding, so the writing word goes round the eating word

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
scoffed in the sense of gobbled food

explanation.surface: Pals mocked something someone had written.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoffed looks like jeered but here means wolfed down; the two letters for writing sit around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mates is everyday British slang for pals or close companions.

clue.text: Charges extra for a degree

parts.note: surface: someone bills more than expected, perhaps excessively
setter's reading: the additional university tuition charges introduced in England

explanation.walkthrough: 'For a degree' sounds like 'to some extent', but it means a university qualification; these were the extra tuition charges brought in for English students in the 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplementary university tuition charges payable by students on top of the basic fee were called this in Britain.

clue.text: Soldier-priest

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a member of the armed services
second meaning, playful: a cleric is the one who leads church services

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen suggests an army chaplain, but the two halves are separate senses: one in the forces, and a man who takes services.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the military is a serviceman; a clergyman conducting church services could whimsically be called one too.

clue.text: New Zealander unable to take off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the informal name for a person from New Zealand

definitions.note: describes the flightless bird rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the national bird, which cannot fly

explanation.surface: A traveller from New Zealand is stuck, perhaps with a grounded plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The national bird of New Zealand is flightless, and its name is used as a nickname for the country's people.

clue.text: Garages get damaged by lots of little stones

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so its letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: the two words taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Car garages are harmed by a hail of gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregates are the gravel and crushed rock mixed into concrete or laid in roads.

clue.text: A lot of horses sent off with toning lotions

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: a string is a group of racehorses kept by one stable
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A stable's horses are dispatched along with skin-care products.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringents are lotions that tighten the skin and close the pores.

clue.text: Heard the artist was about to play role of planner

indicators.note: about in the sense of round, so the painter wraps the performing verb
heard means the painter's name is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: the Venetian painter, whose name rhymes with fish-un
to act is to play a role

explanation.surface: A famous painter was set to take on the part of an organiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian, the Renaissance painter, is spelt here by sound, and the verb for performing goes inside after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactician is someone skilled at devising plans and manoeuvres to reach a goal.

clue.text: Marks the inclusion of a short break for those learning

indicators.note: inclusion means taking something inside, so the break goes within the marks

parts.note: scars are marks left on skin
hol is a shortening of holiday

explanation.surface: A teacher's grades include a brief pause for students.
explanation.walkthrough: Marks looks like grades for students, but means blemishes on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholars are learned people or students, those engaged in study.

clue.text: Support each treatment for pain

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

indicators.note: treatment means processing or working over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A brace or support, with treatment for each patient's pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Support and treatment read as medical care, which suits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Backache is a specific kind of pain felt in the spine or lumbar region.

clue.text: A cleric then danced and got the bird

indicators.note: dancing moves things about, so the letters step into a new order

parts.note: the three words taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman dances and is booed off: getting the bird is British slang for being jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanticleer is the traditional name for a rooster in fables such as Chaucer's tale.

clue.text: Fellow dispersed litre into a purification system

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man pours a measure of liquid into a cleaning device.
explanation.definitionFit: A filter removes impurities from water or air passing through it, cleaning it.

clue.text: Must change, having afterthought on floors

indicators.note: change tells the solver the word must be altered into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as letters to be rearranged
a postscript is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A builder must change the flooring after second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: Floors is a verb, as in 'that question floors me', not the surfaces underfoot.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump someone is to baffle them completely, the same as flooring them with a hard question.

clue.text: Classic trees

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the five English Classic horse races, run at Epsom for fillies
second meaning: plural of a common hardwood tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' looks like an adjective for the trees; it is a noun, one of Britain's five Classic flat races, of which this is the fillies' race at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is a famous English flat race ranked among the Classics, and oaks are also acorn-bearing hardwoods.

clue.text: One who speaks double Dutch?

parts.note: surface: someone talking incomprehensible gibberish
setter's reading: a person fluent in two languages, Dutch being one example

explanation.walkthrough: Double Dutch is an idiom for nonsense, but read literally it is someone who speaks two tongues; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A person fluent in two languages could be described by this rare term for a bilingual speaker.

clue.text: Bury some of the main terrorists

indicators.note: some of means only part, so the answer is a run of letters inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A call to bury several leading terrorists.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave, a formal synonym of bury.

clue.text: Give ground to man in church

indicators.note: in puts the man inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: Yielding territory to a fellow inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield land or rights to another party.

clue.text: Mistakenly claims the golden touch is his

indicators.note: mistakenly means in error, so the letters are set down wrongly and must be reordered

parts.note: the two words taken as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly boasts of turning everything to gold, like Midas.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: an alchemist's claim to turn base metal into gold was always mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: An alchemist sought to transmute ordinary metals into gold, so the power of gold-making was his supposed skill.

clue.text: Mark follows to carry the emblem

indicators.note: follows says the mark comes after the carrying word in the order

parts.note: to tote something is to carry it
M is the abbreviation for the old German mark

explanation.surface: A man named Mark comes next, bearing a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark reads as a man's name but is the currency abbreviation, placed after the verb meaning carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or image serving as the symbol of a clan or group.

clue.text: She has been there to get a drink

definitions.note: describes the place rather than naming it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman has visited a place in order to buy a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, originally in Ireland and South Africa, where alcohol is sold illicitly.

clue.text: New gradings for holiday destinations

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fresh classifications or sortings
second meaning: places people go for vacations

explanation.surface: Tourist spots are given fresh star ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as re-sorts, sortings done again, to see the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Places visited for recreation are resorts, and the same letters split as re-sorts mean fresh sortings.
